Random donor imputation by exact matching

Source: R/matchImpute.R
matchImpute.Rd

Fill missing values by sampling from groups of rows with the same values in the matching columns. Broaden the groups when a donor is unavailable.

matchImpute(
  data,
  variable = colnames(data)[!colnames(data) %in% match_var],
  match_var,
  imp_var = TRUE,
  imp_suffix = "imp"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, data table, or matrix.

variable

Unique column names or positive column positions to impute. Defaults to all columns outside match_var. An empty selection skips imputation and indicator creation.

match_var

Unique matching column names in order of decreasing priority. Use character(0) or NULL to start with all rows in one group.

imp_var

Logical. If TRUE, write a logical indicator for each target column. The indicator is TRUE where the target was originally missing.

imp_suffix

A single character suffix for the indicator names. Each name consists of the target column name or position, an underscore, and this suffix. If a name already exists, choose another suffix or set imp_var = FALSE.

Value

The imputed data as a data table for data table input and as a data frame for data frame or matrix input. Row names are carried over using the standard data frame rules. The count_missings attribute is a matrix with columns STEP and NA_PRESENT. Step 1 records the total number of missing cells across the target columns before imputation. Each subsequent step records that count after one pass.

Details

  1. Group the rows by all columns in match_var. Rows with NA in a matching column can share a group if their other matching values agree.

  2. For each target column within each group, use the non-missing entries in that column as donors. Draw one value uniformly with replacement for each missing cell. If there is only one donor, copy its value to every missing cell in the group. If there are no donors, leave those cells for the next pass. Each target column is imputed separately, so values filled in the same row can come from different donors.

  3. If any target cells are still missing, drop the last remaining matching column and repeat. For example, c("region", "age_group") matches on both columns first, then on region alone, then pools all rows if needed. Each pass fills only cells that are still missing. Values filled in previous passes enter the donor pool for later passes.

Matching columns with many distinct values can produce small groups and lead to broader fallback groups. A target column that is entirely missing causes an error because it has no donor even when all rows are pooled. Use set.seed() before calling matchImpute() to reproduce the random draws.

See also

hotdeck()

Other imputation methods: hotdeck(), impPCA(), imputeCellEM(), imputeCellIRMI(), imputeCellM(), imputeCellMCD(), imputeCellwise(), imputeRobust(), imputeRobustChain(), irmi(), kNN(), medianSamp(), rangerImpute(), regressionImp(), sampleCat(), vimmi, vimpute(), xgboostImpute()

Author

Johannes Gussenbauer, Alexander Kowarik

Examples


data(sleep,package="VIM")
imp_data <- matchImpute(sleep,variable=c("NonD","Dream","Sleep","Span","Gest"),
  match_var=c("Exp","Danger"))

data(testdata,package="VIM")
imp_testdata1 <- matchImpute(testdata$wna,match_var=c("c1","c2","b1","b2"))

dt <- data.table::data.table(testdata$wna)
imp_testdata2 <- matchImpute(dt,match_var=c("c1","c2","b1","b2"))
